implementation_notes: TypeScript's typed server frameworks supply the endpoint: NestFactory.createMicroservice binds a transport, @MessagePattern(pattern) and @EventPattern(name) methods become the receive side, and ClientProxy.send()/emit() the sending side, with serializer/deserializer and retry options owned by the transporter (TCP, NATS, Kafka, MQTT). The decorator method replaces the classic endpoint class, and DI hands it its collaborators; KafkaJS's typed consumer.run({ eachMessage }) is the lower-level alternative when you do not want a framework.
pitfalls: @EventPattern handlers have no reply channel, so an exception cannot be returned to the sender - treat failures as at-most-once unless the transporter provides retries (TCP's retryAttempts/retryDelay).
Request-response (@MessagePattern) creates an extra channel/queue pair per interaction: it is more expensive than event-based messaging and is easy to introduce accidentally.
Serializer/deserializer and transport options live in bootstrap configuration, so switching transports silently changes payload handling; assert the wire contract in tests.
